A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same framework, policy-gradient estimator, and interpolated critic learning algorithm, despite the changed title and terminology. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original bandit simulations, continuous and discretized MuJoCo/DMC evaluations, and critic-learning and actor-target-network ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and additionally reports Gym, MinAtar, and hybrid-control experiments, expanded baseline comparisons, and statistical analyses.

M1.justification: DPPG/DPAC become DA-PG/DA-AC with the central gradient and ICL updates retained. v2 introduces benchmark-specific adaptations: CNN-feature/action outer-product encoding for MinAtar and disabling double Q-networks for Gym (Appendix D.5). Appendix B also specifies optional, unevaluated entropy-regularized update and reward-shaping variants.

E1.justification: v2 retains the bandits and 20 MuJoCo/DMC environments in continuous and discretized forms, while adding four Gym tasks, five MinAtar games with visual observations, and seven parameterized-action hybrid tasks. These substantially expand the evaluated domains, observation types, and action requirements beyond v1's coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds SAC and PPO to continuous-control comparisons and PPO to the retained discretized-control comparisons. Its new Gym/MinAtar evaluations include EAC, DSAC, and DQN, while hybrid evaluations compare against PATD3, PDQN, and HHQN (Figures 3, 5, and 6). AC-RP/AC-LR/AC-ST are retained under reordered names.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce 500,000-step Gym and 5-million-step MinAtar budgets, benchmark-specific network and training settings, and hybrid evaluation using highest-probability discrete actions and continuous means, reporting evaluation returns or success rates (Appendices D–E). Existing MuJoCo/DMC budgets remain one million steps. For retained bandit policy evaluation, the reported batch size changes from 32 in v1 Appendix B.2 to the Table 4 default of 8 in v2 Appendix D.2; this establishes a documentation-level setting revision, not necessarily a rerun.

E4.justification: The existing ICL-versus-standard-update ablation is extended to Gym, MinAtar, and hybrid control (v2 Figures 7, 14, and 16). Representative bandit critic landscapes and discrete training checkpoints are revised. The underlying analysis questions remain largely unchanged, and the actor-target-network and alternative-learning-rate analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use 10 seeds for control tasks, 50 for bandit optimization, and 95% bootstrap intervals with 10,000 resamples. v2 additionally specifies pooling across seed-environment trials and adds two-sided paired t-tests within settings and across seven setting means (Appendix D.8, Table 1). The Gym row's n=30 is unexplained relative to the stated four tasks and 10 seeds.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for new tasks and comparators. Figure 3 shows the newly evaluated SAC ahead of DA-AC on aggregate MuJoCo performance; Figure 6 shows DA-AC with the highest hybrid-control aggregate. Table 1 newly reports an across-setting ICL mean difference of 0.0508 with p=0.0088. Bandit critic landscapes are also replaced, while the principal retained continuous/discretized-control findings largely persist.

T1.justification: The gradient theorem, variance propositions, and convergence bound are retained, including corrections to the cited DPG analysis already present in v1. v2 makes Proposition 3.2's premises more explicit by placing continuity conditions in Assumption 3.1 and explicitly requiring U to be continuous. Much of this consolidates assumptions previously stated in Assumption 4.1, rather than introducing new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The framework, lower-variance estimator, and ICL contributions remain central. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace the TD3-focused empirical summary with competitive or sometimes better performance across continuous, native discrete, and hybrid control. Hybrid evaluation is no longer future work, and the introduction drops v1's claim of performance without hyperparameter tuning.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges that ICL is generally biased because it omits importance weights, explaining its updates as off-distribution learning (Section 4.3). Appendix B adds substantive applicability discussion, including loss of exploitable discrete-action structure and possible planning extensions. Conversely, v1's warning that clipped Gaussian actions can disadvantage AC-RP disappears, although clipping remains documented.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's CleanRL implementation provenance and existing settings, v2 reports a project-specific code release and reproducibility statement. Appendices D–G document new CNN/action encoding, benchmark adaptations, deterministic hybrid evaluation, extensive comparator hyperparameters, and EAC pseudocode. These substantially expand the information available for reproduction; the code link itself was not externally verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds an extensive related-work appendix covering discrete, continuous, hybrid, and representation-driven approaches. It explicitly compares its formulation with Todorov's concurrent D-MDP work and distinguishes its decision boundary from RepRL, positioning its contribution around practical algorithms and empirical breadth. This substantially expands research positioning beyond v1's shorter discussions.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, terminology is systematically changed to distributions-as-actions, and empirical summaries and explanatory passages are edited. Detailed bandit discussion moves to the appendix, and hyperparameters, plots, and pseudocode are reorganized. The main framework-to-estimator-to-ICL narrative and much of the existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn; Figure 4 expands from four to six panels with a shared legend; and Figure 5 replaces its per-task difference panel with a broader four-benchmark aggregate display. v2 adds hybrid-control displays, a statistical-test table, and numerous configuration tables, expands and rearranges appendix learning curves, and relocates bandit plots. These constitute substantial visual and layout revisions.

improvement.justification: v1 supported its diverse-action-space claim primarily through continuous tasks and their discretizations, leaving hybrid evaluation to future work. v2 substantially strengthens that evidence with native discrete, visual, and hybrid tasks and stronger comparators (Sections 5.1–5.4). Expanded reproducibility information, closer research positioning, and explicit acknowledgment of ICL bias further improve transparency. These gains outweigh the removed RP-clipping caveat and the unresolved Gym sample-count inconsistency in Table 1.
